<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ai.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8e0e35c0ac1e92eab384f8ea8e1342c65a2ab7a6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6333265c8cb0325c8292071963ea1092b1469b7f` — the merge of head `84a78148953446d4aa43fa86f270543942bfb3f5` into base `8e0e35c0ac1e92eab384f8ea8e1342c65a2ab7a6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6333265c8cb0325c8292071963ea1092b1469b7f && git checkout 6333265c8cb0325c8292071963ea1092b1469b7f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8e0e35c0ac1e92eab384f8ea8e1342c65a2ab7a6 84a78148953446d4aa43fa86f270543942bfb3f5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8e0e35c0ac1e92eab384f8ea8e1342c65a2ab7a6 && git merge --no-ff 84a78148953446d4aa43fa86f270543942bfb3f5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8e0e35c0ac1e92eab384f8ea8e1342c65a2ab7a6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8e0e35c0ac1e92eab384f8ea8e1342c65a2ab7a6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `84a78148953446d4aa43fa86f270543942bfb3f5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/object-query-source.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts

Read: card #31992 (body, claim 6754723402, triage 6754742221, amendments 6754762328 and 6755280319, dev report 6755683040), parent #31868 and its comments (cloud's shape answer 6754528731 above all), PR #32024 (body, 17 files, net diff against `main` from merge-base `8e0e35c0`), and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `data/filter.zod.ts`, `data/filter-save-door-refusals.ts`, `data/date-range-presets.ts`, `data/query.zod.ts`, `data/data-engine.zod.ts`, `ai/dataset-tools.zod.ts`, `system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts`, `objectql/src/engine-find.ts`, `metadata-protocol/src/protocol-list-query-params.ts`, ADR-0122, ADR-0149, AGENTS.md Post-Task 3.

**Check-runs, read last (2026-11-10T00:57Z): 65 runs, 24 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 31 STILL IN PROGRESS.** Running: Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check UI, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI. Concluded green, among the 24: Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates, Build Docs, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · CI release and engine gates, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · scoped · slot lookup and corpus. ⛔ The verdict below is on the contract. The gate families the running jobs answer (the `Iso_` pin under `tsc`, the spec test suite with the pin count and the new test file, the core build that emits the JSON Schema and reads the dropped-refinement baseline) have no conclusion yet; the seat reads them green before ACCEPT. The PR is also still a draft.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface, `@objectstack/spec/ai`: three new exports, nothing changed or removed. Right.** `ObjectQuerySourceSchema` (const), `ObjectQuerySource` (type, `z.input`), `OBJECT_QUERY_SOURCE_TOOL_NAMES` (const, readonly tuple). `api-surface/ai.json` shows exactly these three and no `ObjectQuerySourceParsed`. The barrel hunk is one `export *` and one doc line. A widening.
- **Accept-set of every existing schema: unchanged. Right.** `FilterConditionSchema` and `AggregationFunction` are imported, never edited (no file under `packages/spec/src/data/` is in the diff). `.optional().describe()` wraps the shared filter schema and does not mutate it. `DatasetProvenanceSchema` is untouched, as the claim's ⛔ requires.
- **New accept-set, member by member against cloud's `ResultSource` (6754528731). Right on every member; four are tighter than cloud's TypeScript type, each judged in ④.**
  - `object` string, required: equal.
  - `label` optional string: equal.
  - `filter` optional: cloud `Record of string to unknown`; spec `FilterConditionSchema`. Tighter (④ F2).
  - `scope` literal `visible_to_you`, required: equal (cloud Q5: one value, a literal type).
  - `groupBy` optional string array: equal.
  - `aggregations` optional array of `{ function, field? }`: `function` is cloud `string`, spec the six-value `AggregationFunction`. Cloud Q5 names exactly `count`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count_distinct`; the enum at `query.zod.ts:161` is exactly those six. Equal in fact. No alias member, as cloud says.
  - `orderBy` optional array of `{ field, order? }`: `order` is cloud `string`, spec `asc | desc`. Tighter (④ F1).
  - `limit` optional: cloud `number`, spec positive integer. Tighter (④ F3).
  - `related` optional string array, `latestPer` optional `{ groupBy, orderField }` both required strings: equal.
  - `records` optional: cloud `number` (a count), spec non-negative integer. Tighter (④ F3). A list is refused, which is cloud's Q4 answer.
  - `line` required string: cloud says at most 280 characters; spec `min(1)` and no maximum. Wider at the top and stated so in the describe; `min(1)` is the one bound cloud did not state (④ F3).
  - No member invented, none of cloud's twelve missing.
- **"Left out, never null": right.** Every optional member is `.optional()`, none `.nullable()` or `.nullish()`; a `null` is refused at that key.
- **Unknown keys: stripped, right.** The root, `aggregations[]`, `orderBy[]` and `latestPer` are plain `z.object`. A result block read from another party's producer is the case for strip, not strict; the sibling `DatasetProvenanceSchema` is plain `z.object` too. `filter` is a record and keeps its keys, as it must.
- **Parsed state: none, right.** No `.default()`, `.transform()`, `.catch()` or `.pipe()` anywhere in the tree. `FilterConditionSchema` is annotated `z.ZodType` with the same type for input and output (`filter.zod.ts:2332`), and its `superRefine` changes no type. So `z.input` equals `z.infer`.
- **Generated artefacts follow from the source and are the lane seat's**: 12 `ai/ObjectQuerySource:*` rows in `authorable-surface/ai.json`, one `filter.lazy` row in `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` (the same site `ai/DatasetProvenance` carries), the manifest, the reference page, the ledger counts, `llms.txt`.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — agreed. Three exports added, no existing accept-set narrowed, no export removed.

`Metadata-protocol: added` with `@objectstack/spec` **minor**: correct. AGENTS.md Post-Task 3 reads "the level follows the kind alone: a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves, `none` takes `patch`". The kind is `added` because `gen:schema` writes the schema's 12 keys into the authorable surface, as it does for every published schema, and `check-changeset-no-major` reads the moved shard as a protocol change (amendment 2, which withdrew amendment 1's `patch`). A tool result is not something a metadata author writes, so `added` is the gate's reading rather than the rule's plain meaning; `minor` is the safe level either way, and a pure export addition would not be wrong at `minor`. The changeset body carries both declaration lines line-initial, matches the PR body, names one package, and is not BREAKING, so no migration and no ADR-0087 disposition are owed. `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` concluded success.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev report (6755683040) has `open_questions: []` and `out_of_scope_findings: []`. Its three deviations:

1. **`Metadata-protocol` briefed `none`, measured `added`, changeset `minor`.** Answered by amendment 2; agreed in ②.
2. **No `ObjectQuerySourceParsed`; an `Iso_` pin instead, count 852 to 853.** Answered by amendment 1; agreed in ④. The claim's original name list (which had `ObjectQuerySourceParsed`) is superseded on the record.
3. **Surface widened by `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` and `llms.txt`.** Answered by amendment 2. The baseline is hand-edited by design (its own description says it has no `gen:` script and the build prints the corrected entry), so amendment 2's "not edited by hand" can only mean "not beyond what the build demanded". The row is the one the build demands and mirrors `ai/DatasetProvenance`. No objection.

Flags this review raises for the seat:

- **Amendment 1 ruling 3 asked this review to check "that cloud's producer cannot emit another spelling" of `orderBy[].order`. Answered in part; the rest is escalated.** Cloud's source is not readable here. What the tree proves: `engine.find` and `findOne` run every `orderBy` node through the strict `SortNodeSchema` (`objectql/src/engine-find.ts:356`), so on the record-read path an engine-accepted direction is `asc`, `desc` or absent. What it does not prove: `aggregate_data` and `visualize_data`, whose "group cut" ordering (cloud's words for `limit`) may be applied by cloud itself, and whether the block echoes the tool's raw input or the engine's node. Cloud's own type is `order?: string`. See ④ F1. The seat confirms with `repo:cloud#2`, or lets the cloud follow-up settle it: once `resultSourceBlock()` is typed as `ObjectQuerySource`, a `string` there is a compile error.
- **The card's item 3 follow-ups have one carrier on the record, not two.** #31868 carries the console switch (its report names `carrier: #31992`). No cloud card for "cloud types its producer against it" is named on #31992, on #31868 or in the dev report. The seat files or names it; F1 and F2 both lean on it.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ai/object-query-source.zod.ts`** — against cloud's answer 6754528731 (the ruling it implements) and its first consumer, #31868's `AnswerSource`. The design holds. Nothing here is a must-fix or a should-fix.

- **F1 · nit · `orderBy[].order` is `asc | desc` where cloud types `string`.** The enum is the right contract: a reader can only draw a direction it knows, and the engine's record-read door admits nothing else. The gap is the unproven half in ③. If cloud can emit `ASC`, or a direction on a group cut the engine never saw, a reader that `safeParse`s the block loses the whole block for one member. No change to this head: the schema states the intended contract, and the cloud follow-up makes the producer meet it at compile time. Carried by ③.
- **F2 · nit · `filter` reuses `FilterConditionSchema`, which is an authoring door, and it is not exactly "as the engine accepted it" in one corner.** I tried cloud's whole Q3 list against it:
  - Every listed operator passes: the schema is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` intersected with `$and`, `$or`, `$not`, so no operator key is refused by name (`filter.zod.ts:2332`).
  - A relation filter (`{ project: { client: "id" } }`) passes: the comparand walk does not judge inside a field spec with no `$` key (`depth` above 0).
  - `{today}`-style placeholders pass, in scalar and in `$between` positions: the type face admits a placeholder string, and the preset check matches bare names only, never a braced one.
  - `get_record`'s `{ id: recordId }` passes.
  - What the refinement refuses is what the query faces refuse (`reportQueryFaceRefusals` calls the faces themselves), so a `where` the engine accepted passes, with one exception: a bare date-range preset word (`today`, `this_quarter`, `last_30_days`, 16 names) as a `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte` or `$between` comparand is refused here on ANY field, while the engine refuses it only on a declared temporal field (the schema's own docblock states that boundary). So `{ code: { $gte: 'today' } }` on a text field is accepted by the engine, answered by the tool, and refused in the block.
  - That case has no sensible reading and I do not expect a real block to carry it. The reuse is right (one `where` dialect, the member `DatasetProvenance.runtimeFilter` already uses, as the card asked). Left as an accepted deviation. A reader should treat a block that fails to parse as "no block", not as an error, which is what #31868's lifter already does.
- **F3 · nit · three bounds cloud did not state.** `limit` positive integer, `records` non-negative integer, `line` `min(1)`. Each matches what cloud describes (a top-N cut, a count, a finished citation), and none can refuse a block cloud describes. But the PR body's "no member invented" is true of members, not of bounds, and each bound is one more way a whole block is refused. `object` and `label` carry no `min(1)`, so the file is not uniform on blank strings either. Accepted deviation; no change.
- **F4 · nit · the `label` describe writes one producer's present behaviour into the contract.** "Translated only when the request is in Chinese and a `zh*` translation pack names the object" is accurate to cloud at `4724690b`, and it is what a reader needs to know (the label is not in the caller's UI locale). But it is published as the key's contract in the JSON Schema and the reference page, a second tool author following it would implement "Chinese only", and it goes stale the day cloud detects a second language. The durable sentence is "the authored label unless the producer translated it for the request language; never assume the caller's UI locale". A fix moves the head and the generated output, so it belongs on the cloud follow-up or its own card, not this round.
- **F5 · nit · `OBJECT_QUERY_SOURCE_TOOL_NAMES` is a second list of names the spec already holds.** The five are right: all five are in `PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE['service-ai']` (`platform-tool-names.ts:47-55`) and they are cloud's Q1 list. Nothing ties the two lists together, so a tool renamed or added in the registry leaves this one stale with every test green. A one-line subset assertion in the test would close it. Follow-up; the test file is the lane seat's.
- **Checked and holding, no finding:**
  - `scope` as a closed literal. A second scope value would make an older reader drop the block, which is the right failure: a reader must not print "only records visible to you" for a scope it does not know. The docblock promises older-reader tolerance for added KEYS only, which is accurate.
  - No `kind` discriminant, though the sibling has `kind: 'dataset'`. Cloud's block has none, and the two blocks sit under different keys (`source`, `provenance`). Inventing one would break "no member invented".
  - "It sits beside `DatasetProvenanceSchema`, and the two share members where they mean the same thing" (card item 1). `filter` and `runtimeFilter` share one schema. `label` is deliberately not shared: the dataset label is "at the caller's locale" and this one is not, and the describe says so.
  - `aggregations[].field` optional for every function, though `count_distinct` needs one at the query door. An echo does not re-validate the query.
  - `limit` "present only together with `orderBy`" is describe text, not a refinement. Right: a refinement would add a second dropped-refinement site and nothing a reader needs.
  - The file docblock, sentence by sentence against cloud's Q1 to Q5: five tools, top-level `source`, beside `chart` on `visualize_data`, none on an error result, composed by the tool, sibling of `provenance` under ADR-0149 D3, rule 4's fallback. All agree. `records`, `related`, `latestPer` and `line` describes agree with cloud's wording.

**`packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts`** — one `export *` beside `dataset-tools.zod` and one line in the module list. No name collides (`ObjectKnowledgeSource` is a different name; `api-surface/ai.json` gains three rows and loses none). Holds.

**`packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts`** (implementing: it enforces the no-`Parsed` ruling) — ADR-0122 D3: a schema whose `z.input` and `z.infer` are the same type "must not be given a second name". The tree has no default or transform, so D3 applies and amendment 1's reversal of the claim is correct. The diff adds `M205`, the pin `Iso_ai_objectQuerySource__ObjectQuerySourceSchema`, and moves the count in all three places it is stated (section header, case title, `toHaveLength(853)`). The pin is proved by `tsc`, and `Type Check · workspace` is still running; the count is proved by the spec suite, also still running.

**Not reviewed (lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`):** `object-query-source.test.ts`, the changeset prose, the generated artefacts, `llms.txt`, the baseline. One note for that ACCEPT: the test's `null` loop covers seven optional keys and leaves out `related` and `latestPer`.

Findings: 0 must-fix, 0 should-fix, 5 nits (F1 to F5), all left as accepted deviations or follow-ups. No fix is asked on this head.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-3wun0i`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QsR2jUe9c6YdtNkrzUnMUd`

**VERDICT: PASS**
